meaning_of_resolved: The final contract contains a specific design resolution; live implementation and proof remain required.

findings.title: Archive-wide provenance is incomplete
findings.evidence: Candidate, tracked source, and fixture digest authorities verify, but 249 copied metadata/evidence/research/legacy entries lack a supplied archive-wide digest authority.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Treat those entries as unverified context; preserve assistant-computed digests and never promote them without independent corroboration.

findings.title: Snapshot cannot prove live state
findings.evidence: Archived branch, HEAD, status, worktrees, runtime, plugin installation, and command output are historical observations only.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Ultra must recompute every live precondition before acting or claiming.

findings.title: Candidate law binding is circular
findings.evidence: Candidate wording conditions binding behavior on implemented validators/proof, permitting absent validators to weaken law.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Separate adopted normative status, implementation status, proof eligibility, and claim decision.

findings.title: Candidate requirement trace is too coarse
findings.evidence: The candidate has one row per broad law and cannot localize implementation/proof responsibility.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Replace with granular stable requirement IDs and full source/surface/tool/claim mappings.

findings.title: Current plugin manifest is lane-era
findings.evidence: The snapshot manifest description and routes retain gate/lane product semantics.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Rewrite around plugin journeys and bind manifest contents to package inventory.

findings.title: Plugin draft is not a supported runtime manifest
findings.evidence: The large draft inventory is useful internal data but conflates generated inventory with host plugin wiring.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Use supported manifest fields and generate internal inventories separately.

findings.title: Repo marketplace surface is missing
findings.evidence: Only a personal-marketplace example is present; current repo-scoped marketplace conventions are not implemented.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Add and test repo and personal distribution surfaces independently.

findings.title: Three skills lack required discovery metadata
findings.evidence: agent-improvement-loop, agent-observability-stack, and product-fitness-gate lack required `name`/`description` frontmatter.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Consolidate topology and validate every active skill metadata block.

findings.title: Skill topology duplicates concepts
findings.evidence: Fourteen active skills overlap around fitting, proof/product gates, orchestration, and observability.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Consolidate to eight product-semantic skills with measured legacy routes.

findings.title: Custom agents use the wrong current discovery path
findings.evidence: Snapshot TOMLs live in `custom-agents/`, while current project-scoped Codex custom agents use `.codex/agents/`.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Move canonical read-only roles and verify discovery in a new run.

findings.title: Static write roles overgrant authority
findings.evidence: Static lane-era roles make ownership durable and broad rather than run-scoped and dependency-aware.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Keep custom agents read-only; create explicit disjoint write leases per run.

findings.title: Lane/gate migration is pervasive
findings.evidence: Tracked snapshot includes 13,542 lane references across 872 files and 10,808 gate references across 1,221 files.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Use semantic inventory, compatibility routing, active-reference scans, and staged retirement rather than renaming only visible docs.

findings.title: Hard-coded GPT-5.5 assumptions remain
findings.evidence: Tracked snapshot contains 297 GPT-5.5 references across 172 files.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Classify historical references; capability-probe or parameterize active model assumptions.

findings.title: Public CLI surface is overgrown
findings.evidence: The handwritten `Command` enum exposes 37 variants with overlapping authority and internal terminology.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Collapse to ten product-semantic groups and generate compatibility routes.

findings.title: CLI parse errors may mutate observability state
findings.evidence: The parser error path invokes observability emission, violating no-hidden-write expectations for parsing/read surfaces.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Enforce structural zero-write parsing/help/query behavior and test filesystem/event-store immutability.

findings.title: Handwritten parser increases drift and ambiguity
findings.evidence: Manual parsing duplicates grammar, help, validation, and compatibility logic.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Adopt a typed parser and generate command/effect catalogs.

findings.title: Candidate custom tooling is over-fragmented
findings.evidence: Nineteen candidate tools split tightly coupled authority and invite orchestration overhead.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Consolidate to twelve semantic Harness-owned tools with explicit APIs and proof.

findings.title: Duplicate finalizers and claim authorities remain
findings.evidence: Audit, product, standards, final-packet, and transactional-finalization surfaces can compete.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Make HCT-CLAIMS the sole machine claim authority and retire projections/writers.

findings.title: Proof-shaped output can be rewarded
findings.evidence: Receipts, generated rows, telemetry, and green tests are abundant enough to become optimization targets.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Install explicit surrogate-evidence guards, negative controls, and behavior-grounded scoring.

findings.title: Mutable receipts/current-state files are too authoritative
findings.evidence: State projections and receipts appear across many command-specific flows.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Recompute from typed context-bound facts; treat projections as disposable views.

findings.title: Some host proof requirements are impossible without exposed APIs
findings.evidence: A snapshot or local tool cannot prove host-internal cache, selected model/mode, or undisclosed registry state.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Probe only exposed surfaces, report unknown, and lower dependent claims.

findings.title: Installation and discovery are conflated
findings.evidence: Catalog files, installed bytes, host registration, and runtime selection are not consistently separated.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Implement identity-preserving transition claims from package through runtime.

findings.title: Routine work inherits excessive ceremony
findings.evidence: Lane/gate architecture encourages broad proof on ordinary changes.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Use conservative affected sets and reserve claim-specific strict proof for boundaries.

findings.title: Dirty-tree preservation is not a universal invariant
findings.evidence: Scattered commands may assume clean state or write unrelated artifacts.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Centralize context/effects and test staged, modified, untracked, and worktree cases.

findings.title: Telemetry is at risk of becoming proof authority
findings.evidence: Observability and proof surfaces are tightly intertwined.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Make events diagnostic evidence only; prohibit event rows from setting claims.

findings.title: Plugin hooks and extensions cross trust boundaries
findings.evidence: Plugin components can execute with host permissions and require explicit trust.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Inventory components, minimize them, disclose effects, and test disabled/denied states.

findings.title: Evaluation core is vendor-adapter heavy
findings.evidence: Promptfoo and OpenAI-specific modules risk owning canonical semantics and future deprecation exposure.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Keep vendor-neutral canonical schemas and adapters; migrate deprecated surfaces.

findings.title: Candidate research is already temporally stale
findings.evidence: GPT-5.6, Goal, plugin marketplace, and custom-agent documentation changed by July 10, 2026.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Refresh primary sources and require freshness checks for mutable capability claims.

findings.title: Path-only write scopes cannot prevent semantic collision
findings.evidence: Workers can edit different paths that generate or govern the same authority.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Lease path, semantic symbols, generated outputs, fixtures, and external effects together.

findings.title: Shared authority needs a sole root owner
findings.evidence: Workspace manifests, command catalogs, claim graphs, migration registries, and releases cannot be safely co-owned.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Workers request changes; root applies, integrates, and reconciles.

findings.title: External stop conditions are under-specified
findings.evidence: Signing, distribution, telemetry, licensing, and destructive cleanup require real authority.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Represent them as open decisions with claim-local effects and safe defaults.

findings.title: CLI implementation can crowd out the plugin product
findings.evidence: Repository volume and candidate detail center heavily on validators and receipts.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Make plugin journeys, skill quality, installation/discovery, and fresh-user behavior first-class nodes and claims.

findings.title: Legacy aliases lack complete retirement policy
findings.evidence: Scattered compatibility and historical references do not carry owner, measurement, deadline, or removal proof.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Generate a single migration registry and enforce route lifecycle.

findings.title: Fresh-agent navigation is not proven
findings.evidence: File presence and extensive documentation do not establish comprehensibility or correct route selection.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Run new-task skill/agent/repository journeys without hidden context.

findings.title: Release and completion can be conflated
findings.evidence: A package or green finalizer can be mistaken for integrated product completion.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Use separate claim IDs and exact prerequisites; completion remains root-reconciled.

findings.title: Protected host configuration cannot be leased to workspace-write workers
findings.evidence: Current Codex sandbox documentation protects project `.git`, `.agents`, and `.codex` paths; treating those paths as ordinary worker write scopes creates an impossible or bypass-seeking workflow.
findings.resolution_in_final_contract: Keep protected configuration root-owned. Workers return exact requested changes; the root independently reviews and applies them only through exposed host authority.
